messages:
Sarah - Sales: Hi team — FinEdge is asking for Private deployment networking guidance. They want on-prem clients to connect through their edge proxy into our Private connector. Key asks: preserve client source IP for their firewall allowlists, preserve SNI for logging, and minimize changes to their perimeter. Also asked for rough pricing delta between using VPC peering vs PrivateLink + NAT.
Alex - Solutions: Quick clarifying q: is the on-prem -> cloud path over a Site-to-Site VPN/DirectConnect to their VPC, or terminating to a transit/VPN vendor?
Sarah - Sales: They have an S2S VPN to a spoke VPC behind a TGW. They prefer not to stand up new NATs if possible.
Mike - NetOps: Short answer: VPC peering (or routed via TGW) preserves original source IPs. PrivateLink (interface endpoints) will not preserve original client IP because traffic terminates at the ENI and then is proxied into the service, so you'll see endpoint ENI IPs as source.
Eli - Security: Thanks — also SNI is part of the TLS ClientHello, so if the customer does TLS passthrough it's preserved. If they do TLS inspect (mitm), SNI may be rewritten/removed depending on the device.
Jordan - SE: For the allowlist requirement, options: 1) Use VPC peering / TGW routing so backend sees client src IPs (no NAT). 2) If using PrivateLink, they must allow the endpoint ENI IP ranges (we can provide CIDR list) or use our connector with preserved-srcip mode using a NAT instance with source preservation — but that requires additional infra and may change egress cost.
Sarah - Sales: Can you give a short firewall snippet they can hand to their net team?
Alex - Solutions: Yep, example (they'll need to replace placeholders):
```
# allow outbound from customer spokes to Redwood connector
allow tcp from 10.20.0.0/16 to 52.208.100.0/24 ports 443,9443
# if using PrivateLink also allow interface endpoint ENI CIDRs (we will supply exact ranges)
```
Mike - NetOps: Note on SNI preservation with PrivateLink: if the client terminates TLS to our service (no TLS inspect), SNI is preserved end-to-end. If the vendor TLS-inspects at the edge, SNI may be removed — ask them to add an exception for traffic destined to Redwood to bypass TLS inspection.
Sarah - Sales: Pricing question from customer: how much more expensive is PrivateLink+NAT vs simple peering? They care about egress units + added NAT instance cost.
Jordan - SE: Rough rules: peering/TGW routing has no extra AWS interface endpoint charges and will have only normal data transfer pricing. PrivateLink has hourly ENI/endpoint costs + per-GB data processing on some clouds; plus if you add NAT instances for source preservation you should budget EC2 NAT + EIP costs and transfer through NAT. For Redwood side: Private deployment connector itself doesn't change token pricing but could change network egress paths which affects cloud egress.
Eli - Security: Also raise that some regulated customers require explicit IP ranges for allowlists. We can provide a short-lived set of connector IPs for the POC but for production they'll want a stable architecture (peering with stable CIDRs or Dedicated reserved capacity).
Sarah - Sales: Customer scale: expecting ~120 RPS steady, occasional spikes to 800 RPS, average request size ~1.5k tokens. Will that push them towards Dedicated / reserved?
Jordan - SE: 120 RPS steady with spikes is modest but bursty. For POC we can run on shared hosted, but for stable SLA + predictable costs recommend Dedicated capacity. Pricing/commit depends on 95th percentile throughput; I'll add a rough calc once we have target p95 latency and token mix.
Alex - Solutions: Action items: 1) Mike to run a quick connectivity test via TGW peering to confirm src IP behavior and share tcpdump. 2) Eli to draft TLS inspection guidance and allowlist wording. 3) Jordan to produce a back-of-envelope cost delta (peering vs PrivateLink+NAT) for Sarah to share in the next call. 4) deploy-bot to attach the Private deployment networking runbook.
Mike - NetOps: I'll spin up a tiny test in their spoke (with their creds) tonight and post results. Expect a pcap + `curl --resolve` test showing preserved src IP. :white_check_mark:
Eli - Security: I'll drop a one-pager with the exact phrasing: "Bypass TLS inspection for connections to Redwood connector / allow SNI passthrough" and example firewall lines.
deploy-bot: Attached -> https://redwood.docs/runbooks/private-deploy-networking (runbook) :link:

Sarah - Sales: Awesome, please keep notes minimal — customer wants a single page they can hand to NetSec. If we can give them a 1-page decision matrix (Peering vs PrivateLink tradeoffs + estimated monthly delta) that would be ideal.
Jordan - SE: Will do. I'll aim to have the one-pager + cost delta by EOD tomorrow and tag this thread.
Sarah - Sales: Thanks everyone. I'll book the follow-up 30m with FinEdge after we have the packet capture and the one-pager. :calendar:
